content:
Dear Halden Pay Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role. Across nine years in data engineering, including work in payments, I have built and operated production data platforms and warehouses that support finance, risk, analytics and product teams. I am particularly drawn to Halden Pay’s focus on reusable platform capabilities and its values of ownership, collaboration and moving quickly by reducing unnecessary complexity.

At Lukovac Freight Hub, I own the ingestion layer of a platform with around 140 Airflow DAGs and have helped make its warehouse more reliable and efficient. I moved transformation logic into dbt, with tests across 420-plus models, reducing the nightly build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. I also introduced data contracts with CI checks, reducing broken-pipeline incidents, and built a Kafka-based streaming pipeline processing around 30 million events per day. These projects have involved operating production systems, improving data quality and making platform interfaces more dependable for the teams that use them.

My experience at Kovalent Pay also gives me a direct connection to Halden Pay’s payments work. I built PySpark jobs on AWS EMR to reconcile bank settlement files with internal ledgers, processing about 1.2 TB per day and reducing month-end manual reconciliation from around three days to four hours. I designed a Redshift dimensional warehouse used by finance and risk, and added data quality checks to critical finance tables. My cloud experience is with AWS, including managed data services such as EMR, S3 and Redshift; I would bring that production experience alongside my Python, SQL, Airflow and dbt background.

I value open-source practice and knowledge-sharing: I have contributed fixes and tests to a community Airflow provider, mentor two data engineers, and have spoken at a regional data meetup about data contracts. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience building reliable, reusable data platforms could support Halden Pay’s Data Platform team.

Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well tailored to Halden Pay’s Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role. It presents strong evidence through quantified achievements: 140 Airflow DAGs, 420-plus dbt models, 30 million streaming events per day, 1.2 TB per day, and major reductions in runtime and manual reconciliation effort. The payments experience is especially relevant, and the references to reusable platforms, open-source contribution, mentoring, and data contracts fit the role well. The main content weakness is that it does not explicitly demonstrate advanced Python and SQL or large-dataset query optimisation, despite the candidate’s material supporting relevant evidence. Data modelling is mentioned through the Redshift dimensional warehouse, but could be made slightly more prominent.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses a standard, parsing-friendly structure with a clear salutation, role title, company name, conventional paragraphs, and no problematic tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting. It includes important terms such as data platform, production systems, Airflow, dbt, Kafka, PySpark, AWS EMR, S3, Redshift, Python, SQL, data quality, data contracts, and open-source. ATS and AI screening alignment would improve if the letter explicitly used the job description’s terms “production data platforms,” “cloud data warehouses at scale,” “data modelling,” “query optimisation,” “reusable frameworks,” and “data quality standards.” Do not add Google Cloud technologies, graph modelling, or Portuguese because the candidate information does not support them.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a strong match for designing, building, and operating production data platforms at scale, cloud data warehousing, Airflow/dbt, data quality, payments, and open-source practices. It also aligns with Halden Pay’s Together, Ownership, and Pace values through collaboration with product teams, mentoring, ownership of ingestion, operational improvements, and reducing unnecessary complexity. AWS is a credible comparable cloud background, although it is not Google Cloud. The candidate’s material supports stronger evidence for Python/SQL optimisation and cost/performance engineering than the letter currently presents. Graph modelling and Portuguese are not supported by the candidate material and are gaps or optional gaps rather than document defects.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE: In the third paragraph, after the sentence ending “data quality checks to critical finance tables,” add a concise sentence that explicitly connects the evidence to the requirement for large-dataset optimisation, for example: “This work required writing production Python and SQL for large datasets and optimising data processing and warehouse performance; at Lukovac, I also reduced the Snowflake bill from approximately $38K to $24K per month through warehouse sizing, auto-suspend, and removal of unused tables.” Ensure the wording remains accurate and does not claim a specific SQL optimisation technique not documented in the candidate material.

HIGH-VALUE: In the second or third paragraph, make the modelling evidence more explicit by changing “I designed a Redshift dimensional warehouse used by finance and risk” to “I designed a Redshift dimensional warehouse using a star schema with more than 30 fact and dimension tables, used by finance and risk.” This uses the job description’s “data modelling” terminology while remaining fully supported.

MINOR: In the second paragraph, change “I own the ingestion layer of a platform” to “I own the ingestion layer of a production data platform” and change “These projects have involved operating production systems” to “These projects have involved designing, building, and operating production data-platform capabilities.” This more closely mirrors the role’s screening language without adding unsupported experience.

MINOR: In the final paragraph, replace “open-source practice” with “open-source practices” and retain the specific Airflow provider contribution and merged pull requests. This matches the job description’s wording more closely.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, and well targeted to the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role. It uses strong, quantified evidence: 140 Airflow DAGs, 420+ dbt models, 30 million events per day, 1.2 TB per day, and measurable improvements to build time, reconciliation effort, incidents, and cloud cost. The payments experience is particularly relevant to Halden Pay. The letter also credibly addresses ownership, platform reliability, open-source practices, mentoring, and collaboration. A minor weakness is that some claims are slightly indirect—for example, “have helped make its warehouse more reliable and efficient”—despite the candidate having clear ownership and measurable results. The letter could also connect more explicitly to the ad’s wording around production operation, reusable platform capabilities, data modelling, and comparable cloud experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is highly parseable: it uses standard headings-free paragraphs, conventional text, no tables or graphics, and includes relevant keywords such as data platforms, warehouses, Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Kafka, AWS, EMR, S3, Redshift, data quality, open-source, and production. AI screening probability is high because the document directly names the target role and presents quantified, role-relevant evidence. For stronger keyword alignment, it could use the exact phrases “designing, building and operating production data platforms,” “data modelling,” “query optimisation,” “reusable platform capabilities,” and “comparable cloud.” Only add “query optimisation” if the candidate can substantiate that work; the supplied material clearly supports warehouse and processing optimisation, but does not specifically document SQL query tuning.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns very well with the role. It shows production data-platform ownership through the ingestion layer, Airflow orchestration, dbt transformation, Kafka streaming, Snowflake operations, on-call participation, and data contracts. It shows payments-domain relevance through bank settlement reconciliation, internal ledgers, finance, risk, Redshift, and large-scale PySpark processing. Strong data modelling is shown by the Redshift star schema with 30+ fact and dimension tables. AWS is a credible comparable-cloud background through EMR, S3, Redshift, Glue, and Snowflake operations. Curiosity about architecture and open-source practices is supported by data contracts, CDC, an Airflow provider contribution, and the data-contracts presentation. The values connection to Ownership, Together, and Pace is credible, although the letter could tie those values more directly to concrete examples. The document does not show graph modelling or Portuguese; the candidate information does not establish either capability, so these are genuine requirement gaps rather than document defects.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the second paragraph, replace “I own the ingestion layer of a production data platform with around 140 Airflow DAGs and have helped make its warehouse more reliable and efficient” with the more direct, evidence-based wording: “I design, build, and operate the ingestion layer of a production data platform with around 140 Airflow DAGs, while improving warehouse reliability and efficiency.” This better mirrors the job description without overstating the candidate’s responsibilities.

2. In the second paragraph, change “These projects have involved designing, building, and operating production data-platform capabilities” to “These projects involved designing, building, and operating reusable production data-platform capabilities for product, analytics, and operational teams.” This uses the employer’s “reusable platform capabilities” terminology and is supported by the candidate’s platform work and stated users.

3. In the third paragraph, change “I designed a Redshift dimensional warehouse using a star schema with more than 30 fact and dimension tables” to “I designed and operated a dimensional Redshift warehouse using a star schema with more than 30 fact and dimension tables.” Use “operated” only if the candidate was responsible for its ongoing production use; the supplied experience supports production ownership of the warehouse design and related data-quality checks.

4. In the third paragraph, replace “This work required writing production Python and SQL for large datasets and optimising data processing and warehouse performance” with “This work required production Python and SQL for large datasets, distributed processing, and warehouse-performance optimisation.” This is more specific and ATS-friendly while remaining supported by the PySpark, EMR, Redshift, Snowflake cost, and build-time evidence. Do not describe this as “SQL query optimisation” unless the candidate can substantiate direct query-tuning work.

5. In the final paragraph, add the candidate’s open-source testing detail by changing “I have contributed fixes and tests to a community Airflow provider” to “I fixed a pagination bug and added tests to a community Airflow provider, with two pull requests merged.” This provides stronger evidence for the job’s open-source-practices requirement and remains concise.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, focused cover letter with a professional tone and clear relevance to Halden Pay's Data Platform role. It demonstrates senior-level scope through quantified results: 140 Airflow DAGs, 420-plus dbt models, 30 million streaming events per day, 1.2 TB per day, and significant reductions in processing time, reconciliation effort, and Snowflake cost. The payments experience is especially well connected to Halden Pay's business. The letter also addresses the company's stated values, reusable platform capabilities, open-source practices, and knowledge-sharing. Its main opportunity is to make a few job-ad terms more explicit, particularly dimensional data modelling, query optimisation on large datasets, and day-to-day platform operation.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS- and AI-screening-friendly: it uses standard paragraphs, a conventional greeting and closing, no tables or unusual formatting, and includes strong keywords such as Senior Data Engineer, data platform, Airflow, dbt, Kafka, Python, SQL, AWS, EMR, S3, Redshift, data quality, data contracts, open source, and production. AI screening probability is high for the core requirements because the evidence is specific and quantified. Matching could improve slightly by using the exact phrases "dimensional data modelling," "query optimisation," and "designing, building and operating production data platforms." The website at the end is useful, although it would be marginally clearer as a labeled contact link such as "Portfolio: lenavh.dev."
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with the role. It shows experience designing, building, and operating production data platforms at scale; Python and SQL work on large datasets; dimensional warehouse design; AWS as a comparable cloud; Airflow and dbt; data quality practices; reusable platform capabilities; open-source contribution; mentoring; and professional English. The payments reconciliation and finance/risk warehouse experience is a particularly strong match for Halden Pay's fintech context. It also credibly reflects Ownership through operational responsibility and measurable improvements, Together through mentoring and cross-team work, and Pace through reducing complexity and cycle time. Graph modelling and Portuguese are gaps in the candidate information, but they are nice-to-have requirements and do not represent defects in this cover letter.
critique.improvement_instructions:
Minor enhancement 1 — In the third paragraph, immediately after the sentence about designing the Redshift dimensional warehouse, add an explicit supported phrase such as: "This gave me hands-on experience with dimensional data modelling for finance and risk workloads." This makes the ad's exact modelling requirement easier for ATS and recruiters to identify.

Minor enhancement 2 — In the third paragraph, revise the sentence beginning "This work required writing production Python and SQL" to: "This work required writing production Python and SQL for large datasets and optimising data processing and warehouse performance." This preserves the existing evidence while making the job ad's query-optimisation requirement more explicit.

Minor enhancement 3 — In the second paragraph, after describing the Kafka pipeline, add the supported operational evidence: "I also participate in a one-week-in-six data-platform on-call rotation, reinforcing my experience operating production platform services day to day." This strengthens the exact "design, build and operate" match without adding unsupported experience.

Minor enhancement 4 — In the closing paragraph, change "I value open-source practices and knowledge-sharing" to "I value open-source practices, reusable platform design and knowledge-sharing." This more directly connects the existing open-source contribution and platform experience to the role's focus on reusable frameworks.
